title: “They’ve Been Using YOUR Signature Against You | UCC 1-308 Explained”
summary: Promoter video claiming your signature creates credit, that signing 'all rights reserved UCC 1-308' avoids debtor status, and that UCC-1 filings make you the secured party.

assertions.quote: You can sign your name. All rights reserved UCCC1-308.

verdicts.note: UCC 1-308 preserves objections in commercial performance; it does not release a signer from a contract's obligations.
1-308 only keeps rights a party reserves while it performs or assents to performance; it is about continuing performance despite a dispute, not escaping the obligation as debtor.

assertions.quote: It's not just a country. It's a corporate jurisdiction governed by commercial law.
You are the issuer of the credit, the living man behind the legal fiction

verdicts.note: Courts reject 'vapor money' and 'you created the credit' theories; the borrower owes the loan.
The claim that the borrower creates the loaned money by signature is called erroneous; the one supporting case (Credit River, 1968) was declared a nullity and rejected in Commonwealth courts.

assertions.quote: And in contract law, nondisclosure equals fraud by omission.

verdicts.note: Truth in Lending requires disclosure of credit terms, not this theory; courts dismiss nondisclosure-of-credit-creation claims.

assertions.quote: I'll show you how to file your UCCc1 financial statement, how to notify agencies that you are the secured party

verdicts.note: The court calls the strawman and redemption theory behind such UCC filings 'equal parts revisionist legal history and conspiracy theory' and 'clearly nonsense in almost every detail'.
Filing UCC-1 statements with birth certificates to 'redeem' the straw man is a frivolous redemption theory that courts call implausible and clearly nonsense.

assertions.quote: you have the right to dispute any alleged debt within 30 days and demand full accounting

verdicts.note: The FDCPA gives a 30-day validation right against third-party collectors, but not against original creditors and not to a 'full accounting'.
